title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #100 review (api-stocks-indicator-history)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #100 (api-stocks-indicator-history), tracked here so they aren't lost once that PR merges and its comments scroll out of view.

checklist.step: backend/app/signals/engine.py's analyse_history() is O(range_size x full_history_length) -- each per-bar analyse() call recomputes EMA/MACD/Elder-Ray/Stochastic/Force-Index (plus up to 5 extra evaluate_wave calls via _wave_lookback) from scratch over an increasingly large slice, synchronously in the request handler. Accepted as a documented tradeoff for the default range=1y, but range=max is an explicitly supported, tested input and a real multi-second-plus latency risk for tickers with several years of daily history. Consider a caching layer or an incremental (non-recompute-from-scratch) implementation.

backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py:339 -- `bar_date.date() if hasattr(bar_date, "date") else bar_date` guards a branch that can't currently occur (daily_ohlcv.index is always a DatetimeIndex of pd.Timestamps by this point), so the else is dead code that gives false protection. Either drop the hasattr guard (call .date() directly) or add a comment explaining why it's defensive, and confirm a future non-Timestamp index would fail loudly (Pydantic validation) rather than silently passing through.

decisions.decision: Worked this task from the actual task JSON's checklist state (item 1, the O(range_size x history_length) analyse_history() performance item, was the real remaining `done: false` item; item 2, the dead hasattr branch, was already `done: true` -- and confirmed already removed from backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py in PR #100's own second round, per that PR's commit history) rather than the dispatch instruction's summary, which had the two items' done/remaining status backwards. No code change was needed or made for item 2; this PR's entire diff addresses item 1.
decisions.rationale: The task file (the authoritative source per CLAUDE.md's task-board rules) and the actual repository state (backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py:340 already reads `date=bar_date.date()` with no hasattr guard anywhere in the file, confirmed via `git show` on the PR #100 merge commit) both directly contradicted the dispatch summary. Re-doing an already-completed, already-verified fix would have been wasted/risky busywork; leaving the genuinely open O(n^2) performance item undone would have left the task incomplete despite the dispatch text's framing.

decisions.decision: Fixed the O(range_size x history_length) cost by precomputing every causal/rolling-window indicator analyse_history() needs exactly once over the full (cleaned) daily_ohlcv/weekly_ohlcv, then passing analyse() a cheap positional .iloc[:k] slice of each precomputed series per bar instead of letting analyse() (and, transitively, _wave_lookback/evaluate_wave/evaluate_tide) rederive them from each bar's own truncated window. Extended this to all five indicators the checklist item named (EMA(13)/EMA(26)/MACD-Histogram/Stochastic-%K/Force-Index-2EMA, via new optional keyword params on analyse()/evaluate_wave()/_wave_lookback()) plus, after profiling showed it was actually the next-largest remaining cost, Screen 1 (Tide)'s own weekly EMA(13)/EMA(26)/MACD-Histogram (new optional weekly_ema_13/weekly_ema_26/weekly_histogram params on analyse(), forwarded to evaluate_tide()'s pre-existing like-named params from the portfolio-exit-rules-followups task) and the redundant per-bar drop_malformed_daily_bars rescan (a new private analyse(..., _daily_ohlcv_already_clean=True) escape hatch used only by analyse_history(), which already cleans the full frame once up front). Did not further optimize _weekly_through_bar_date's own boolean-mask construction or the volume-rolling-average call inside analyse()'s confidence-scoring branch -- both are real per-bar costs but were not named in the checklist item and profiling after the above fixes showed neither stands out as a remaining O(n) time sink (verified via cProfile at n=2000/4000 bars; scaling from n=1000 to n=4000 daily bars is now linear, ~2x time per 2x bars, not quadratic).
decisions.rationale: The five named daily indicators were the checklist item's explicit target and the biggest cost by far in an initial profile (~2x wall-clock improvement alone). But profiling after that first pass showed Screen 1's weekly-side recompute and the redundant drop_malformed_daily_bars rescan had become the new dominant costs (together >50% of remaining time) -- leaving them unaddressed would have left the checklist item's own stated concern ("a real multi-second-plus latency risk for tickers with several years of daily history") only partially resolved. All three additions reuse the same established, already-precedented pattern in this codebase (evaluate_tide/evaluate_impulse's own optional precomputed-series parameters, from the portfolio-exit-rules-followups task) rather than inventing a new caching layer or duplicating any Screen/signal logic -- lower risk than the alternative of maintaining a second, parallel implementation of analyse()'s orchestration just for the history endpoint. Chose a private (leading-underscore) keyword-only parameter for the drop_malformed_daily_bars skip specifically, rather than making it public, since it depends on a caller-provided guarantee (already-clean input) that only analyse_history() can actually prove -- an ordinary public caller must not be able to opt out of the safety check by mistake. Measured net effect: analyse_history() over a synthetic 2000-daily-bar/~400-weekly-bar series dropped from ~6.0s to ~1.4s (a ~4.3x speedup), with linear (not quadratic) scaling confirmed up to 5000 bars (~3.6s) -- verified via a throwaway benchmark script (not committed) comparing against the pre-change implementation checked out via `git show`.
decisions.alternatives_considered: A full caching layer (e.g. per-ticker memoized indicator series keyed by a cache invalidation policy) was rejected as unnecessary complexity for a single-request code path with no cross-request reuse need -- the existing app.data.cache module already handles the actual cross-request caching concern (raw OHLCV fetches), and this task's cost is pure in-process recomputation, not I/O. Skipping the weekly-Tide and drop_malformed_daily_bars optimizations (stopping at just the five named daily indicators) was considered and rejected after profiling showed they'd become the dominant remaining cost, per the rationale above.

comments.summary: analyse_history()'s new top-level drop_malformed_daily_bars() call (added so the precomputed indicator series and every per-bar slice agree on which rows exist) is a genuine, currently-dormant behavior change for a caller passing not-fully-cleaned data with a malformed bar in the *middle* of history: that date's entry is now silently omitted from the returned history entirely, instead of (pre-PR) still being emitted with the prior clean bar's values. Reproduced directly (60-row synthetic frame, row 30 malformed: pre-PR returns 60 entries including one for the malformed date, this PR returns 59). The only real caller (app/api/routers/stocks.py) already pre-cleans before calling analyse_history, so there is no live production effect today, and the new behavior may even be more correct -- but it's undocumented and untested. Non-blocking; filed as a follow-up.

The docstring/decisions' O(range_size x history_length) -> O(history_length) total framing is not strictly accurate: elder_bull_power/elder_bear_power (High/Low - EMA(13)) are still computed fresh per bar over each truncated slice, not precomputed-and-sliced like the five daily + three weekly indicators this PR did precompute -- so, on top of the already-acknowledged per-bar volume-rolling-average and weekly boolean-mask costs, the function's true worst-case complexity remains O(range_size x history_length), just with a much smaller constant. Confirmed empirically this doesn't matter in practice: a synthetic worst-case benchmark engineered to maximize Wave-screen rolling-std recomputation still showed clean linear scaling from n=500 to n=4000 (0.53s/1.01s/2.06s/4.04s). Documentation-precision nit, not a live performance bug. Non-blocking; filed as a follow-up.

code-review skill (dispatched separately, converged independently) pinpointed the concrete mechanism behind the complexity nit above: _is_force_index_spike's force_index_2ema.rolling(window=13).std() recomputes the rolling std over the *entire* slice it's handed (not just the trailing window) before taking .iloc[-1], so each call remains O(len(slice)) rather than O(1). Since _wave_lookback can invoke this up to 6x per bar whenever the Stochastic-threshold condition already holds, a ticker/range where Wave crosses OVERSOLD/OVERBOUGHT often enough could still see close-to-quadratic total cost, though my own worst-case-engineered benchmark (an oscillating bullish-tide series with volume spikes, maximizing how often this branch fires) still scaled linearly to n=4000. Non-blocking; folded into the same follow-up task alongside the elder_ray finding above, with a concrete one-line fix suggested (slice force_index_2ema to its trailing _FORCE_INDEX_SPIKE_WINDOW bars before .rolling().std()).

review.notes: Full review per the PR-reviewer process. Checked out PR #121 (branch already current). Backend test suite: 570 passed, 99.86% overall coverage, 100% on both touched modules (engine.py, triple_screen.py) -- no coverage regression, well above the 90% gate. ruff + mypy clean on backend; frontend untouched by this PR (no lint/tsc run needed, last known state clean). code-review skill launched in the background for an additional pass and completed before finalizing this review -- it converged independently on the same underlying complexity-claim gap identified manually (see the third comment above, which folds its more precise finding into the same follow-up as the manually-found elder_ray one) and raised no other findings after 8 review angles including its own regression run (209 signals-suite tests). Also did an independent manual code-review + verify-elder-signal walkthrough directly (no signal/confidence/risk methodology logic touched -- purely an internal recompute-once-and-slice refactor via new optional keyword params, all defaulting to prior behavior; Screen 1/2/3, Impulse gate, and confidence weights/logic are byte-for-byte unchanged). Independently spot-checked correctness beyond the PR's own regression tests: wrote a standalone script computing analyse_history() over a 300-bar synthetic series and cross-checking signal/confidence/indicators/screens at 12 historical indices (including two weekly-boundary-crossing dates) against a fresh analyse() call on the same truncated slice -- zero mismatches. Verified no look-ahead directly: perturbed a bar 5 days after a checked index by +1000 and confirmed the checked index's result was byte-identical before/after (precomputed-series slicing at index N provably only reflects data through bar N, confirmed both by this test and by reading ema()/macd_components()/stochastic_oscillator()/force_index() -- all are causal/trailing-window, never centered or forward-looking). 'Last point matches /analysis' invariant reconfirmed both via the existing test and my own spot-check at index 299. The private _daily_ohlcv_already_clean escape hatch is safe: it's only ever set by analyse_history() itself after that function has already cleaned the full frame once up front, so every per-bar truncated slice it skips re-cleaning is provably already clean -- confirmed via a targeted test with a malformed bar in the middle of an otherwise-uncleaned input, which showed the top-level clean call still correctly excludes it from every downstream computation. No API route/schema touched -- backend/openapi.json regeneration not applicable. UI-facing: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators has a frontend consumer (the stock-detail indicator-history chart), so ran the full browser walkthrough despite no route/schema change: started backend (FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture) + frontend dev servers, drove /stocks/AAPL with a Playwright script (no dedicated Playwright browser tool was available in this session, so used the project's own installed playwright-core directly as an equivalent substitute) -- 1Y and MAX ranges both render the price/EMA chart and all three oscillator panes correctly, zero console errors, zero failed network requests; also checked the invalid-ticker edge case (clean 'Not found' state). Also ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e): all 13 specs passed, including stock-analysis.spec.ts's dedicated 'selecting the Max range does not crash the oscillator pane or the app (PR #108 review regression)' spec, which directly exercises this PR's own performance-optimization code path. No checklist item phrased as 'decide X' was left undecided -- both decisions entries (task-worker's scope-correction and the optimization design itself) are present and substantive. Two non-blocking findings recorded above and filed as docs/tasks/api-stocks-indicator-history-followups-followups.json.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran the backend suite: 570 passed, 99.86% coverage, 100% on engine.py/triple_screen.py -- matches review's reported numbers exactly. Read engine.py/triple_screen.py in full and confirmed ema()/macd_components()/stochastic_oscillator()/force_index() are all causal (ewm(adjust=False), rolling, diff() -- trailing-window only, never centered/forward-looking), so precomputing once over the full series and slicing .iloc[:k] is provably equivalent to recomputing on each truncated prefix. Reproduced two independent checks beyond the review's own script: (1) loaded origin/main's pre-PR engine.py/triple_screen.py side-by-side with this branch's and ran analyse_history() on the same fixed 300-bar synthetic series through both -- byte-for-byte identical signal/confidence/indicators/screens at every one of 300 bars, confirming this PR is a pure performance refactor with zero behavioral change; (2) my own future-bar-perturbation test (independent script, not the review's) -- perturbed a daily bar 5 sessions after a 400-bar cutoff by +1000 and re-ran analyse_history(), confirming all 400 earlier bars' results were unaffected. ruff+mypy clean. Skimmed the full diff (engine.py, triple_screen.py, test_engine.py, task JSONs, index.json) -- no signal/methodology logic touched, follow-up task and index.json mirroring both correct. skill is null (not add-indicator), so no hand-computed reference value check applies.
